q1_issues.issue: "more often" is a frequency comparative, but it is stuffed into (Manner (sk_happen $x) more_often) as an invented multi-word filler — the instruction set reserves Manner for a surface adverb, encodes comparison with More/MoreBy, and encodes frequency with Every/TimesPer, so the comparison is lost entirely.

"happen" with a non-volitional subject is given Agent, though the intransitive-subject test points at an undergoer role (the thing does not initiate the happening); the "when unclear, Agent" fallback is the only cover.

q2_gaps: comparative with an elided standard ("more often", "faster" with no "than ..." phrase) — every comparative form in the instruction set requires an explicit second argument, so there is no licensed encoding when the standard is implicit (here, an unstated earlier rate)
comparison of FREQUENCY — the frequency machinery (Every / TimesPer) has no comparative or trend form, so "happens more often now" cannot be stated as a rate ordering
notes: The generic rule form, its 0.9/0.9 truth value, the Skolem-function event and the anaphor-with-no-antecedent witness classed "thing" are all correct, and (Like $x sk_thing_1) is licensed as the entity-attached preposition-named oblique. Only the "more often" encoding misrepresents the sentence.
